title: Is there any point to public broadcasting now?

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: The licence fee is frozen again, which is a cut, and the argument is that nobody under thirty watches it anyway.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Watches the channel, maybe. They use the apps and the news site constantly without noticing whose they are.

turns.speaker: Fergal
turns.text: Which is a real measurement problem. The brand is invisible when the content arrives through somewhere else.

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: So how do you justify a compulsory payment for something people don't know they're using?

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: The market failure case is the strongest one. Nobody funds local reporting commercially any more, because it never paid for itself.

turns.speaker: Fergal
turns.text: Council meetings, courts, planning committees. There are places with no reporter in the room at all now.

turns.speaker: Fergal
turns.text: And you find out what that costs about four years later.

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: The flat fee is regressive though, and it's enforced with criminal penalties in some places, which is extraordinary for a television.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: That's the part I'd change rather than the institution. Fund it from general taxation.

turns.speaker: Fergal
turns.text: Which makes it dependent on a minister's goodwill every year.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Unless the settlement is fixed for a long period by statute, which is how the better systems do it.

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: The impartiality obligation is the other thing worth keeping. Everything else in the market is funded by attention.

turns.speaker: Fergal
turns.text: And attention rewards heat rather than accuracy, reliably.

points: A frozen licence fee amounts to a cut, justified by low viewing among under-thirties.
Hana argues younger audiences use the apps and news site without recognising the provider, creating a measurement problem.
The strongest justification is market failure, particularly in local reporting of councils, courts and planning, which never paid commercially.
Zeke objects that a flat fee is regressive and criminally enforced in some jurisdictions.
Hana would fund it from general taxation with a long statutory settlement to avoid annual political dependence.
They value the impartiality obligation, since attention-funded media rewards heat over accuracy.
